name: Apparent magnitude difference
notes: Fluxes compared in the same passband.

name: Monochromatic AB magnitude
notes: The reference flux density uses the same units as F_nu.

name: Photometric colour index
notes: Two passbands for the same source.

name: Distance modulus
notes: Used in the Pantheon+ observation model.

name: Frequency-density K correction
notes: First form. L_shifted is the spectral luminosity evaluated at (1+z) times the observed frequency.

name: Spectroscopic redshift
notes: Wavelength form of the redshift definition.

name: Point-mass gravitational potential
notes: Zero potential at infinity.

name: Specific energy in a potential
notes: Newtonian particle energy per unit mass.

name: Keplerian circular speed
notes: First expression for circular motion in a Newtonian point-mass potential.

name: Keplerian angular frequency
notes: Second expression in the same set of circular-orbit identities.

name: Keplerian specific angular momentum
notes: Third expression in the same set of circular-orbit identities.

name: Keplerian circular-orbit binding energy
notes: Fourth expression. Total specific energy including kinetic and potential terms.

name: Two-body relaxation to orbital timescale
notes: Coulomb-log estimate for stars of common mass m and number density n.

name: Virial potential-energy estimate
notes: Order-of-magnitude estimate for a galaxy of characteristic radius R.

name: Virial speed estimate
notes: Final expression, derived from the same virial mass estimate.

name: Schwarzschild massive-particle effective potential
notes: Includes the rest-energy term in the author's specific-energy convention.

name: Weak-field perihelion advance
notes: Per orbit, written with aphelion radius and eccentricity.

name: Schwarzschild innermost stable circular orbit
notes: Test-particle orbit around a nonrotating compact object.

name: Polytropic equation of state
notes: K is a model parameter and n is the polytropic index.

name: Dimensionless polytropic density
notes: Density member of the dimensionless-variable definitions.

name: Dimensionless polytropic pressure
notes: Pressure member of the dimensionless-variable definitions.

name: Polytrope length scale squared
notes: Scale used to define the dimensionless radial coordinate.

name: Lane–Emden solution for index one
notes: Regular solution, extended continuously to theta=1 at xi=0.

name: Lane–Emden solution for index zero
notes: Constant density interior.

name: Lane–Emden solution for index five
notes: Regular solution with no finite first zero.

name: Pressure gradient in hydrostatic equilibrium
notes: Algebraic RHS of the Lagrangian stellar structure equation.

name: Radius gradient in mass coordinates
notes: Algebraic RHS of the Lagrangian stellar structure equation.

name: Radiative temperature gradient in mass coordinates
notes: Algebraic RHS for radiative diffusion.

name: Local luminosity production per unit mass
notes: Algebraic RHS. The source uses the net local heating rate per unit mass.

name: Stefan–Boltzmann surface flux
notes: Effective temperature is defined through the emergent bolometric flux.

name: Blackbody stellar luminosity
notes: Rearranges the displayed equality to isolate L.

name: Grey atmosphere temperature to the fourth power
notes: Eddington approximation at small optical depth.

name: Radiative thermal conductivity
notes: Rosseland-mean diffusion approximation.

name: Planck spectral energy density
notes: Per unit ordinary frequency. The common dnu is cancelled.

name: Planck specific intensity
notes: Isotropic specific intensity expressed in terms of spectral energy density.

name: Bolometric blackbody energy density
notes: Local thermodynamic equilibrium.

name: Electron-scattering opacity for an ionised mixture
notes: Hydrogen mass fraction X. Opacity is in cm²/g.

name: Eddington luminosity in terms of opacity
notes: Electron scattering supplies the opacity in this source.

name: Eddington luminosity for ionised hydrogen
notes: Pure hydrogen and Thomson scattering.

name: Newtonian thin-disc surface flux
notes: Zero torque at the inner edge. The source takes Mdot negative for inflow.

name: Newtonian thin-disc luminosity
notes: Integral result from both disc faces, with negative Mdot for inflow.

name: Specific energy in the Paczyński–Wiita potential
notes: Circular orbit in a pseudo-Newtonian potential.

name: Alpha-disc viscosity prescription
notes: Dynamical viscosity. The model parameter alpha lies between zero and one.

name: Isothermal spherical wind sonic radius
notes: Same sonic condition for the isothermal inflow and outflow branches.

name: Isothermal gas sound speed squared
notes: mu_H is the mean mass per gas particle in the source's pressure law.

name: Steady thin-disc mass flux
notes: Vertically integrated expression. Negative v_r denotes inflow.

name: Schwarzschild radius
notes: A horizon for a black hole and a characteristic length for other masses.

name: Schwarzschild photon-sphere radius
locator: §1.3.5, maximum of the null effective potential
notes: Radius of the unstable circular light orbit.

name: Weak-field deflection by a point mass
notes: Leading term at impact parameter b much larger than the gravitational radius.

name: Schwarzschild Kretschmann scalar
notes: The notes use c=1.

name: Reissner–Nordström outer horizon
notes: Plus branch. Charge parameter e_geom is the quantity called e in the source's c=1 units.

name: Reissner–Nordström inner horizon
notes: Minus branch with the same charge convention.

name: Equal-mass binary gravitational-wave power scaling
notes: Scaling in units with c=1. Orientation and numerical factors are suppressed.

name: Planck luminosity
notes: Reference power scale used for the gravitational-wave estimate.

name: Sérsic surface-brightness profile
notes: Central intensity convention used in the notes.

name: Exponential galaxy light profile
notes: Spiral-disc case and Sérsic index n=1.

name: de Vaucouleurs surface-brightness profile
notes: Elliptical-galaxy case with central intensity convention.

name: Schechter galaxy luminosity function
notes: Density per unit luminosity.

name: Navarro–Frenk–White halo density contrast
notes: Output is rho(r)/rho_crit.

name: NFW halo characteristic overdensity
notes: c200 is halo concentration, not the speed of light.

name: NFW normalised squared circular speed
notes: x is r/r200 and c200 is halo concentration.

name: Mestel disc surface density
notes: Razor-thin disc with constant circular speed.

name: Tully–Fisher luminosity scaling
notes: Approximate luminosity scaling for rotationally supported spiral galaxies.

name: Faber–Jackson luminosity scaling
notes: Approximate luminosity scaling for dispersion-supported elliptical galaxies.

name: Stellar-disc Toomre stability parameter
notes: Here expressed as the ratio to the critical radial dispersion.

name: Reduced gravitational deflection angle
notes: Scalar component of the source's vector equation.

name: Critical lensing surface mass density
notes: Angular-diameter distances to the lens and source and between them.

name: Einstein radius of a point mass
notes: Point lens with angular distances.

name: Source angle for a point lens
notes: Signed one-dimensional angular coordinate.

name: Outer point-lens image position
notes: Plus solution of the point-lens equation.

name: Total point-lens magnification
notes: u is the positive source separation in units of the Einstein angle.

name: Singular isothermal sphere density
notes: Isotropic constant one-dimensional dispersion.

name: Singular isothermal sphere projected density
notes: xi is projected physical radius.

name: Isothermal sphere Einstein radius
notes: Source on the symmetry axis.

name: Friedmann equation with curvature
notes: Source uses energy density rho and a curvature length R_curv. This display excludes a separate Lambda term.

name: Matter–curvature–Lambda expansion law
notes: E=H/H0. Neglects radiation.

name: Flat late-time Lambda CDM expansion law
notes: Flat specialisation of the source's Eq. (14), squared and multiplied by H0². Neglects radiation.

name: Constant-w cosmological energy-density scaling
notes: The source uses a(t0)=1. Sets the redshift exponents of the expansion law.

name: Flat single-fluid scale factor
notes: Flat single-fluid solution for w≠−1 in the range where the source's Big Bang normalisation applies.

name: Einstein–de Sitter scale factor
notes: Pressureless flat matter-only case.

name: Friedmann acceleration equation
notes: Output is the second time derivative of a divided by a.

name: Present critical cosmological energy density
notes: Uses energy density rather than mass density.

name: Present critical cosmological mass density
notes: Energy-density expression divided by c².

name: Low-redshift Hubble–Lemaître relation
notes: Local recession-speed relation.

name: Hubble distance
notes: Characteristic background distance scale.

name: Angular-diameter distance from transverse comoving distance
notes: D_M is transverse comoving distance.

name: Luminosity distance from transverse comoving distance
notes: First equality of the source's three-way identity.

name: Distance duality relation
notes: Alternative form in the same identity.

name: Constant-w fluid equation of state
notes: rho is energy density. The standalone constitutive relation has no expansion-rate dependence.

name: CMB temperature under free expansion
notes: Radiation remains thermal as photon frequencies redshift after last scattering.

name: Thermal photon number density
notes: zeta_3 denotes the fixed value ζ(3).

name: Thermal photon energy density
notes: Blackbody energy coefficient expanded in physical constants.

name: Hydrogen binding energy from mass difference
notes: m_H is the mass of a ground-state hydrogen atom.

name: Nonrelativistic equilibrium species number density
notes: Dilute Maxwell–Boltzmann regime with chemical potential mu_i.

name: Saha equilibrium relation in the early universe
notes: Output is (1−X_e)/X_e². eta is the baryon-to-photon ratio.

name: Bose–Einstein occupation
notes: Occupation of one state.

name: Fermi–Dirac occupation
notes: Changes the sign in the denominator relative to the Bose form.

name: Free neutron decay after decoupling
notes: Uses the source's approximate initial neutron-to-proton ratio of 1/5.

name: Jeans gravitational growth timescale
notes: m times n_bar is the background mass density.

name: Jeans length in a static fluid
notes: Physical wavelength with background mass density m*n_bar.

name: Primordial matter power-law spectrum
notes: Spectral index n is a model parameter.

name: Dimensionless power per logarithmic wavenumber
notes: Uses the source's Fourier convention and output Delta.

name: Fourier transform of a spherical top-hat
notes: Continuous limit W(0)=1.

name: Parametric spherical-collapse radius
notes: Closed top-hat collapse parameter tau. The source identifies this with the closed matter-only cosmological solution.

name: Parametric spherical-collapse time
notes: Companion time relation from the same parametric solution.

name: Star–planet orbital separation
notes: f is true anomaly and a is the relative semimajor axis.

name: Sky-projected orbital separation
notes: Sky-plane coordinates use the source's choice for the ascending node.

name: Transit impact parameter
notes: Conjunction approximation in units of stellar radius.

name: Occultation impact parameter
notes: Superior conjunction variant.

name: Geometric transit probability
notes: Plus branch includes grazing eclipses. Isotropic viewing angles within the range in which the probability does not saturate at one.

name: First-to-fourth contact transit duration
notes: Circular orbit. k is the planet-to-star radius ratio.

name: Quadratic limb darkening
notes: mu is the direction cosine with respect to the local surface normal.

name: Transit depth including nightside emission
notes: Uniform stellar brightness approximation.

name: Planetary atmospheric scale height
notes: Isothermal ideal gas. mu_m is the mean mass per particle and g_local is local gravity.

name: Rossiter–McLaughlin velocity amplitude
notes: Peak amplitude in the approximation of the source.

name: Pulsar characteristic age
notes: Spin-down age estimator in the dipole model.

name: Pulsar magnetic-field scaling
notes: Dipole scaling with period and its time derivative.

name: Cold-plasma pulsar timing delay
notes: Inputs are frequencies in GHz and dispersion measure in pc cm⁻³. Output is in ms.

name: Keplerian binary pulsar mass function
notes: Mass and inclination form in the right-most member of the source equality.

name: Binary pulsar relativistic periastron advance rate
notes: Masses are in solar units. T_sun=G*M_sun/c³.

name: Binary pulsar Einstein delay parameter
notes: Combines time dilation and gravitational redshift in the GR timing model. Masses are in solar units.

name: Binary pulsar gravitational-radiation orbital decay
notes: Leading GR loss of orbital period in the source's solar-mass convention.

name: Lyman-series flux attenuation
notes: F_unabsorbed is the unattenuated continuum at the appropriately shifted frequency or wavelength.

name: Resonant line absorption cross section
notes: Gaussian-cgs convention. phi_offset is the normalised line profile evaluated at nu−nu0.

name: Lyman-alpha optical depth in a matter-dominated background
notes: Matter-dominated and narrow-line approximation. Uses a specific background expansion law.

name: Thermal free–free spectral emissivity
notes: Nonrelativistic thermal plasma in cgs. The emissivity is per unit frequency and solid angle. g_ff is the frequency-dependent Gaunt factor.

name: Bolometric thermal free–free emissivity
notes: Frequency-integrated form in cgs per unit solid angle. g_ff_bol is the frequency-averaged Gaunt factor.

name: Thermal free–free absorption coefficient
notes: Coefficient in inverse centimetres. The source derives it from the emissivity via Kirchhoff's law.

name: Low-frequency free–free absorption coefficient
notes: Rayleigh–Jeans limit h*nu much smaller than kB*T. The coefficient is in inverse centimetres.

name: Synchrotron cooling time
notes: Uses the total electron energy and power averaged over isotropic pitch angles. beta is the electron speed divided by c.

name: Pitch-angle averaged synchrotron power
notes: Single electron with isotropically distributed pitch angles. U_B is magnetic energy density.

name: Synchrotron critical frequency
notes: Substitutes nu_s from Eq. (4.14). Gaussian-cgs convention and relativistic electrons. theta is the pitch angle.

name: Typical synchrotron frequency
notes: Characteristic frequency estimate for a relativistic electron at a right angle to the field, in Gaussian-cgs units.

name: Inverse-Compton electron energy-loss power
notes: Positive loss power for isotropic seed photons in the Thomson regime. U_rad is the incident radiation energy density.

name: Kennicutt–Schmidt star-formation law
notes: Central fit. Sigma_unit is one solar mass per square parsec. The output is in solar masses per year per square kiloparsec.

name: Orbital star-formation law
notes: Omega_gas is the galactic gas orbital angular frequency. Use consistent units of area and time.

name: Sheth–Tormen halo multiplicity
notes: The left side is nu times f(nu), with nu=(delta_c/sigma)**2 and nu_prime=a_halo*nu. Treat the fluctuation amplitude and collapse threshold as supplied inputs.

name: Press–Schechter halo multiplicity
notes: The source recovers this limit with a_halo=1, p=0 and A_halo=1/2 in its squared peak-height convention.

name: Tinker halo multiplicity
notes: Empirical multiplicity function in the source's f(sigma) convention. The fit coefficients depend on the halo overdensity definition and calibration epoch.

name: Sheth–Tormen Eulerian halo bias
notes: Large-scale bias at the halo formation epoch. nu is squared peak height and delta_c is the linear collapse threshold.

name: Binary chirp mass
notes: Mass combination for the two components. Use a common mass frame.

name: Leading-order inspiral frequency evolution
notes: Left side is f_GW**(-8/3). Valid for a quasi-circular inspiral at leading order. Frequency, chirp mass and time are all in the detector frame.

name: Leading-order inspiral frequency derivative
notes: Solves the source's chirp-mass relation for the frequency derivative. Companion to the integrated frequency evolution.
